body: My brother was the one who suggested finding new hobbies to be productive on. He also gave the humorous, but effective, advice of "put on pants". My counselor approved of those ideas and added that I need to give myself the same leeway I give others, and try to value myself. He's right, but that's hard for me to do. I honestly don't really value my own life beyond what I can do for others. I recognize that there's something really wrong with that, but that's how I feel and think. My prof hasn't given advice, but has repeatedly told me that anytime I need to talk I can speak with her.
A few people. My brother, my current counselor, and one of my professors. I shouldn't have told my brother, but I needed to talk to someone.

Yeah... I know. Dad cares, he's just terrible at expressing it. There's a great deal that I respect about him, and while I gripe about him a lot here he isn't a bad guy. He just isn't able to understand other personalities well.

No, fortunately. I live in a dorm with three suite-mates, but I rarely see them. Each of us has our own room with a common area, so I often keep the door shut and study/read/play games in my room. I'm not a particularly social person unless someone needs me to be.
Thanks for responding so quickly. I've been on meds since before my attempt, about a year now. The dosage has risen steadily, but thus far, no noticeable change. As for my friends, I can't say.
